newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Savimbi says he will complete peace plan by November.
newsitem.headline: Savimbi says he will complete peace plan by November.

text.p: Angola's opposition UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi, slammed by the Security Council for delaying a peace plan to end two decades of civil war, has told the United Nations he will complete remaining steps in the pact within a month.
The Security Council has threatened to implement sanctions against UNITA after November 20 if it fails to meet its obligations under the pact signed with the government two years ago.

U.N. special envoy to Angola, Alioune Blondin Beye, held three hours of talks with Savimbi at his base in Bailundo on Tuesday -- the first since the Security Council met last Friday in New York and extended its peacekeeping mandate to Angola by two months.

"UNITA has agreed to send to UNAVEM and the joint commission before the end of next week a timetable for the execution of all the remaining steps... which will be completed by November 15," Beye told a news conference on his return to the government- controlled capital Luanda late on Tuesday.
He said Savimbi had reaffirmed his commitment to peace.
More than 63,000 UNITA troops have registered and been disarmed at 15 U.N.-supervised assembly camps around the country, although there are just 50,000 fighters present in the camps.
U.N. figures show that more than 13,000 soldiers have deserted the camps, but the United Nations is insisting that some of the deserters should return to the camps.
Beye leaves Luanda on Wednesday for Zimbabwe, the first stop on a five-country tour including Zambia, Namibia, Gabon and South Africa to inform heads of state on the Security Council's resolutions.
U.S. Ambassador to Angola Donald Steinberg, whose country is one of three overseeing the implementation of the Angolan peace process, travelled to Bailundo with Beye for the meeting with Savimbi.
U.S. Under Secretary of State for African Affairs George Moose had been due to meet Savimbi on Monday but had to cancel because of bad weather.
